result:
Done. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (4 tests, 3 files) both pass, and `bunx guren check` reports 11 passed / 0 failures.

The endpoint's code was all present — `routes/admin.ts` exported `registerAdminRoutes()` (which mounts `GET /admin/posts` → `AdminPostController.index` inside a `.middleware('auth')` group), and `AdminPostController` already built the JSON, but nothing ever called the registrar, so the path was never added to the router and fell through to the 404 handler. I wired it up in `routes/web.ts:6,22` — importing `registerAdminRoutes` and calling it with the aliased `router` right after `registerAuthRoutes(router)`, so it inherits the same `'auth'` alias (`requireAuthenticated({ redirectTo: '/login' })`) the rest of the signed-in-only routes use, which gives guests the `/login` redirect instead of a 404. No controller or middleware behavior changed. I re-ran `bun run codegen`, which picked the new named route up into `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` as `admin.posts.index`, and added `tests/controllers/AdminPostController.test.ts` (the path `guren check` looks for) covering the guest redirect and a signed-in request returning both posts newest-first with their embedded `author`.
